judgements.justification: B's Reviewer_69AE based its 'firm no' partly on two wrong claims (PCA inconsistent with Definition 1; the infinite gradient is overfitting), and ATkA's wrong 'Gaussian likelihood only' scope claim reached B's meta-review; A's one wrong claim (9TAc on 1/γ) did not affect its score.
A's spotlight follows unanimous 7, 7, 8 (mean 7.33); the AC concurred with the reviewers rather than setting a tier above them.
A's high ratings all carry confidence 4 and rest on specific checks, such as e4Tf's quantifier point; no enthusiasm-only review.
The authors conceded to B only that the claims should be limited to lossless settings and offered a narrower Definition 1; they confirmed to A only that Theorem 4 is an existence result.

A learned that Theorem 4 holds only existentially and that Eq. (6) is not generic, yet accepted promised rewordings on trust and asked only for 'slightly more careful quantification'; nobody asked to see the revised text.
Scores rose after the rebuttal in both committees (e4Tf in A; ATkA, f5mJ, 69AE in B).
Only B raised the single unrepeated CelebA experiment with no sparsity measure, the degenerate zero-reconstruction case for VAEs and the missing prior-work section, and B's AC used these.

Both committees saw the claims overreach Theorem 4 and the dependence on Dai and Wipf (2019); A treated this as camera-ready edits, B's AC as 'a serious issue for a theoretical work' needing 'a major revision'.
B's AC presented 69AE's VAE-applicability objection as the reviewers' shared view ('they were not convinced'), though ATkA wrote 'In contrast to reviewer 69AE', and the AC posted nothing of its own.
B's Reviewer_f5mJ raised to 6 'after analysing all discussions' without taking part in them.
No sign the authors misread or ignored a reviewer; 69AE, not the authors, left the exchange unanswered.
69AE's review is inattentive but not thin: it makes specific claims, posted twice and adjusted its score, and ATkA challenged it; R28 names its mechanism.
B's AC rejected on final ratings 6, 6, 6, 5 with three of four above threshold and ATkA 'will not oppose accepting'; no score moved down to back the decision.
B's AC stated no positive view of its own and did not decide by a score threshold.
69AE's 5 rests on VAE applicability, which is central to the paper's claims, not peripheral.
Both committees evaluated the paper as a theoretical analysis of VAE/AE objectives.
A's reviewers all had confidence 4 and engaged the theory; no reviewer said the core was outside their expertise.
The extra demands in B (precise claims, prior-work comparison) are the same weaknesses weighted differently (R08), not a different bar for the paper type.
No praise in A rests on a wrong checkable claim.
69AE moved up from a 'firm no' to 5 after retracting its 'bad paper' claim; no reviewer kept the same score after conceding its main concern.

A's AC accepted the promised extension of Theorem 4 for the camera-ready; B's AC called the same changes 'a major revision' requiring resubmission, and ATkA would not rate high without seeing the revision.
ATkA's 'will not oppose accepting' matches its 6; no stance diverged from a score.
No extra reviewer was called in.
Background shaped premise objections in B, not clarity verdicts; reviewers in both committees found Definition 1 (ii) hard to read.
f5mJ raised with a stated reason; no rating rose against its own text.
B's AC did not set aside 69AE; it adopted 69AE's objection.
A's Reviewer_e4Tf rated 8 at confidence 4 after a detailed reading that found the Theorem 4 quantifier gap; B had no rating above 6 and stage 1 notes 'no champion'.

added.name: Partial-reading reviewer claimed high confidence
added.definition: A reviewer in one committee admitted reading only part of the paper yet rated with high or top confidence, and that review's objections set the tone or entered the decision.
added.justification: R12 covers a thin review that does not engage; 69AE engaged and made specific claims, but rated with top confidence a paper it admittedly had not finished, a separate failure no reason names.

added.name: Reviewer's theoretical school contested the premise
added.definition: Reviewers in one committee read the paper from a different theoretical tradition than its own and made the premise or framing a central objection, while the other committee's reviewers accepted the framing and judged the results within it.
added.justification: R24 covers expertise distance shaping clarity verdicts and R16 different kinds of contribution; neither names reviewers whose own school of thought made them reject the paper's premise.

reasoning: Stage 1 finds both committees agreed on the facts but priced the same overclaiming differently (R08): A accepted promised fixes on trust (R05, R21), while B's AC rejected 6, 6, 6, 5 ratings as needing a major revision (R13) and presented 69AE's objection as everyone's (R09). Each side heard different concessions (R04), B alone raised the thin experiment and VAE degeneracy (R07), f5mJ moved on the others' discussion (R10), wrong claims fed B's criticism (R01), and A had a checked 8 with no B counterpart (R27). Two causes lacked a reason: 69AE's top-confidence review of a half-read paper (R28), and B reviewers' theoretical school turning the framing into a premise objection (R29).
